The materials used for this investigation were hot-extruded Mg-2.8Nd-0.2Zn-0.5Zr (wt.%) alloy rods with an initial diameter of ~5.3 mm. The as-cast ingots were first solutionized at 540 ◦C for 8 h. And then the as-extruded rods were obtained by extrusion at 300 ◦C with an extrusion ratio of 72:1.

In this work, the JDBM alloy rod with superior strength-ductility synergy was prepared by single-pass drawing at an elevated temperature of 500 ◦C after extrusion.

After hot drawing at 200, 350 or 500 ◦C respectively, the average sizes of grain and particles reduced, LAGBs increased by about 11 times, twins increased sharply, GNDs density increased by 5~6 times, and a nearly basal texture was formed.

After hot drawing at 200, 350 or 500 ◦C respectively, the average sizes of grain and particles reduced, LAGBs increased by about 11 times, twins increased sharply, GNDs density increased by 5~6 times, and a nearly basal texture was formed.
Single-pass drawing at elevated temperatures with a pass reduction ratio of 29 % could significantly enhance the mechanical properties of the as-extruded JDBM alloy rods.
